elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Inserted paragraph: "Garman shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Sparkling and its affiliates..." — express defend obligation running to Customer and affiliates, curing the original clause which only said "indemnify ... and hold it harmless" with no defence duty.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: "...hold harmless Sparkling and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting Losses, to the extent arising out of..." The original ran only to Sparkling and its officers/directors.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Limb (i): "an allegation that the Work or the Maintenance Services infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right" — allegation-level trigger covering both the deliverable (Work) and the services, unlike the retained clause which triggered only on a holding of infringement/breach of the title warranty.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Limb (iii): "any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Sparkling's data or Confidential Information caused by Garman" — the agreement has no defined "Customer Data" term, so describing the data by reference to Sparkling's data/Confidential Information is a reasonable operative anchor.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Limb (iv): "Garman's gross negligence or wilful misconduct" — both categories present.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: "Sparkling shall notify Garman of any such claim". Note the retained ten-calendar-day notice condition applies to the original warranty-breach indemnity; the new notice obligation is unqualified and does not contradict it.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: "Garman shall control the defence and settlement of the claim" — control expressly allocated to Vendor.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: "Sparkling shall provide reasonable cooperation in the defence".

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: "Sparkling's indemnity obligations, if any, under this Agreement are limited to third-party claims arising out of content provided by Sparkling and Sparkling's breach of applicable law" — operative cap on the Customer-side indemnity; no broader Customer indemnity exists elsewhere in the cited text to contradict it.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Original clause covers Losses from breach of the title/quiet-enjoyment warranty and infringement of another Person's rights; the added limb (i) squarely covers third-party IP infringement/misappropriation claims.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no modification exclusion is present, and none is required. Absence is Customer-favourable, so the condition does not apply.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no combination exclusion appears in Section 13 as rendered; its absence favours Customer and does not defeat the element.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no Customer-specification exclusion is present; the condition does not apply.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: Retained limbs (a)-(c): procure the right to use the infringing element, procure an equivalent element, or replace/modify so it no longer infringes.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: Limbs (a)-(c) are the only remedies; Garman need only "make every reasonable effort" and there is no refund/termination-with-refund backstop where none of (a)-(c) is achievable. To reach the fallback the drafter would have to add a fourth limb (e.g. "(d) if none of (a)-(c) is commercially reasonable, terminate the affected licence and refund the fees paid for the affected Work").

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No super-cap is stated; Section 15 expressly disapplies the liability limitation to breaches of Section 13, so the indemnity is uncapped. Literally unmet, but the absence is more favourable to Customer than the fallback and should not be 'repaired'.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Not a fallback element; covered above at the preferred level by limb (iii).

reasons: All ten preferred elements are met in operative language by the single inserted paragraph: defend/indemnify/hold harmless for Customer and affiliates, the four trigger limbs (IP allegation, breach of law, Vendor-caused unauthorised access/disclosure, gross negligence/wilful misconduct), the notice/control/cooperation procedure, and an express cap on any Customer-side indemnity. The preferred level is therefore position-complete and the finding is correctly classified as a deviation targeting the preferred position.

The fallback level is not complete (no refund backstop where procure/modify/replace fail; no 3x super-cap), but that is immaterial because only one level need be met — and the drafter's choice not to import the super-cap is sound, since Section 15 already disapplies the liability limitation to Section 13, leaving the indemnity uncapped in Customer's favour.

Minimality holds: nothing existing is deleted or paraphrased, the favourable retained (a)-(c) remedies and the uncapped Section 15 carve-out survive, and the insertion adds no survival tail, expense allocation, extra damages categories or procedures beyond the notice/control/cooperation mechanic the checklist requires. Reuse of the defined term "Losses" avoids introducing a new damages basis, and referencing "Sparkling's data or Confidential Information" is justified because the agreement defines no "Customer Data" term.

Intent is preserved: no dangling cross-reference or undefined term is created (Work, Maintenance Services, Losses and Confidential Information are existing contract terms), the ten-day notice condition on the original warranty-breach indemnity is untouched and operates alongside the new procedure, and the Section 15 exclusive-remedy/consequential-damages allocation is unchanged.

Drafting note for the drafter (not a defect at the targeted level): the new paragraph's unqualified "Sparkling shall notify Garman of any such claim" sits next to the retained ten-calendar-day notice condition; if Vendor argues the ten-day condition applies to the new limbs, consider an express "promptly (and the ten-day condition above shall not apply to this paragraph)" clarifier in negotiation.
